hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: The matter agreed upon among us regarding the mudabbar (slave promised freedom upon master's death) is that his owner may not sell him nor transfer him from the position in which he placed him. If debts overwhelm his master, the creditors cannot sell him while his master lives. If his master dies with no debt upon him, then he (the mudabbar) is freed from one-third of the estate, because he stipulated his service as long as he lives. It is not permissible for him to have his service during his life, then free him from the heirs' shares after his death from the capital of his wealth. If the master of the mudabbar dies with no wealth other than him, one-third of him is freed and two-thirds remain for the heirs. If the master of the mudabbar dies with debt that encompasses the mudabbar, he is sold for his debt, because he is only freed from the third. If the debt only encompasses half of the slave, half of him is sold for the debt, then one-third of what remains after the debt is freed. Malik said: The sale of a mudabbar is not permissible, nor is it permissible for anyone to purchase him, except that the mudabbar may purchase himself from his master, and that would be permissible for him. Or someone may give the master of the mudabbar wealth and his master who made him mudabbar frees him, and that would also be permissible for him. Malik said: His loyalty belongs to his master who made him mudabbar. Malik said: The sale of the mudabbar's service is not permissible, because it is gharar (uncertainty), since it is not known how long his master will live, so that is an invalid gharar. Malik said regarding a slave who is between two men, and one of them makes his share mudabbar: They should evaluate him, and if the one who made him mudabbar purchases him, all of him becomes mudabbar. If he does not purchase him, his tadbir is nullified, unless the one who still has ownership in him wishes to give his partner who made him mudabbar his value. If he gives him his value, that becomes binding upon him, and all of him becomes mudabbar. Malik said regarding a Christian man who made his Christian slave mudabbar and the slave accepted Islam. Malik said: He is separated from the slave, and the slave pays tribute to his Christian master, and he is not sold until his matter becomes clear. If the Christian dies while in debt, his debt is paid from the price of the mudabbar, unless his wealth is sufficient to cover the debt, in which case the mudabbar is freed.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا فِي الْمُدَبَّرِ ، أَنَّ صَاحِبَهُ لَا يَبِيعُهُ وَلَا يُحَوِّلُهُ عَنْ مَوْضِعِهِ الَّذِي وَضَعَهُ فِيهِ ، وَأَنَّهُ إِنْ رَهِقَ سَيِّدَهُ دَيْنٌ ، فَإِنَّ غُرَمَاءَهُ لَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى بَيْعِهِ مَا عَاشَ سَيِّدُهُ ، فَإِنْ مَاتَ سَيِّدُهُ وَلَا دَيْنَ عَلَيْهِ فَهُوَ فِي ثُلُثِهِ ، لِأَنَّهُ اسْتَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ عَمَلَهُ مَا عَاشَ ، فَلَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يَخْدُمَهُ حَيَاتَهُ ، ثُمَّ يُعْتِقَهُ عَلَى وَرَثَتِهِ إِذَا مَاتَ مِنْ رَأْسِ مَالِهِ ، وَإِنْ مَاتَ سَيِّدُ الْمُدَبَّرِ وَلَا مَالَ لَهُ غَيْرُهُ عَتَقَ ثُلُثُهُ وَكَانَ ثُلُثَاهُ لِوَرَثَتِهِ ، فَإِنْ مَاتَ سَيِّدُ الْمُدَبَّرِ وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ مُحِيطٌ بِالْمُدَبَّرِ ، بِيعَ فِي دَيْنِهِ ، لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا يَعْتِقُ فِي الثُّلُثِ ، قَالَ : فَإِنْ كَانَ الدَّيْنُ لَا يُحِيطُ إِلَّا بِنِصْفِ الْعَبْدِ ، بِيعَ نِصْفُهُ لِلدَّيْنِ ، ثُمَّ عَتَقَ ثُلُثُ مَا بَقِيَ بَعْدَ الدَّيْنِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 لَا يَجُوزُ بَيْعُ الْمُدَبَّرِ ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَهُ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَ الْمُدَبَّرُ نَفْسَهُ مِنْ سَيِّدِهِ ، فَيَكُونُ ذَلِكَ جَائِزًا لَهُ ، أَوْ يُعْطِيَ أَحَدٌ سَيِّدَ الْمُدَبَّرِ مَالًا وَيُعْتِقُهُ سَيِّدُهُ الَّذِي دَبَّرَهُ ، فَذَلِكَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَيْضًا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَوَلَاؤُهُ لِسَيِّدِهِ الَّذِي دَبَّرَهُ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 لَا يَجُوزُ بَيْعُ خِدْمَةِ الْمُدَبَّرِ ، لِأَنَّهُ غَرَرٌ إِذْ لَا يُدْرَى كَمْ يَعِيشُ سَيِّدُهُ ، فَذَلِكَ غَرَرٌ لَا يَصْلُحُ /10 . وَقَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْعَبْدِ يَكُونُ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلَيْنِ ، فَيُدَبِّرُ أَحَدُهُمَا حِصَّتَهُ : /10 إِنَّهُمَا يَتَقَاوَمَانِهِ ، فَإِنِ اشْتَرَاهُ الَّذِي دَبَّرَهُ   كَانَ مُدَبَّرًا كُلَّهُ ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَشْتَرِهِ انْتَقَضَ تَدْبِيرُهُ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ الَّذِي بَقِيَ لَهُ فِيهِ الرِّقُّ ، أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ شَرِيكَهُ الَّذِي دَبَّرَهُ بِقِيمَتِهِ ، فَإِنْ أَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ بِقِيمَتِهِ لَزِمَهُ ذَلِكَ ، وَكَانَ مُدَبَّرًا كُلَّهُ /10 . وَقَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ نَصْرَانِيٍّ دَبَّرَ عَبْدًا لَهُ نَصْرَانِيًّا فَأَسْلَمَ الْعَبْدُ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يُحَالُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْعَبْدِ ، وَيُخَارَجُ عَلَى سَيِّدِهِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ ، وَلَا يُبَاعُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ أَمْرُهُ ، فَإِنْ هَلَكَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ ، قُضِيَ دَيْنُهُ مِنْ ثَمَنِ الْمُدَبَّرِ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي مَالِهِ مَا يَحْمِلُ الدَّيْنَ ، فَيَعْتِقُ الْمُدَبَّرُ /10 .7E427

hadiths.english_translation: Malik narrated that it reached him that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz judged regarding the mudabbar when he causes injury, that his master has the right to hand over what he owns of him to the injured person, so the injured person employs him in service and settles with him for his injury from the compensation of his injury. If he fulfills this before his master dies, he returns to his master. Malik said: The practice among us regarding the mudabbar who causes injury, then his master dies with no wealth other than him, is that one-third of him is freed, then the compensation for the injury is divided into thirds. One-third of the compensation falls upon the third that was freed of him, and two-thirds fall upon the two-thirds that are in the hands of the heirs. If they wish, they hand over what they have of him to the owner of the injury, and if they wish, they give him two-thirds of the compensation and keep their share of the slave. [The narration continues with Malik's detailed legal exposition on mudabbar liability, inheritance, and debt priority, citing Quran 4:12]

حَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ /26 عُمَرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ /26 /20 " قَضَى فِي الْمُدَبَّرِ إِذَا جَرَحَ ، أَنَّ لِسَيِّدِهِ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ مَا يَمْلِكُ مِنْهُ إِلَى الْمَجْرُوحِ ، فَيَخْتَدِمُهُ الْمَجْرُوحُ وَيُقَاصُّهُ بِجِرَاحِهِ مِنْ دِيَةِ جَرْحِهِ ، فَإِنْ أَدَّى قَبْلَ أَنْ يَهْلِكَ سَيِّدُهُ ، رَجَعَ إِلَى سَيِّدِهِ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَالْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا فِي الْمُدَبَّرِ إِذَا جَرَحَ ثُمَّ هَلَكَ سَيِّدُهُ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ ، أَنَّهُ يُعْتَقُ ثُلُثُهُ ، ثُمَّ يُقْسَمُ عَقْلُ الْجَرْحِ أَثْلَاثًا ، فَيَكُونُ ثُلُثُ الْعَقْلِ عَلَى الثُّلُثِ الَّذِي عَتَقَ مِنْهُ ، وَيَكُونُ ثُلُثَاهُ عَلَى الثُّلُثَيْنِ اللَّذَيْنِ بِأَيْدِي الْوَرَثَةِ ، إِنْ شَاءُوا أَسْلَمُوا الَّذِي لَهُمْ مِنْهُ إِلَى صَاحِبِ الْجَرْحِ ، وَإِنْ شَاءُوا أَعْطَوْهُ ثُلُثَيِ الْعَقْلِ وَأَمْسَكُوا نَصِيبَهُمْ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ عَقْلَ ذَلِكَ الْجَرْحِ إِنَّمَا كَانَتْ جِنَايَتُهُ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ دَيْنًا عَلَى السَّيِّدِ ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ الَّذِي أَحْدَثَ الْعَبْدُ بِالَّذِي يُبْطِلُ مَا صَنَعَ السَّيِّدُ مِنْ عِتْقِهِ وَتَدْبِيرِهِ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْعَبْدِ دَيْنٌ لِلنَّاسِ ، مَعَ جِنَايَةِ الْعَبْدِ بِيعَ مِنَ الْمُدَبَّرِ بِقَدْرِ عَقْلِ الْجَرْحِ وَقَدْرِ الدَّيْنِ ، ثُمَّ يُبَدَّأُ بِالْعَقْلِ الَّذِي كَانَ فِي جِنَايَةِ الْعَبْدِ ، فَيُقْضَى مِنْ ثَمَنِ الْعَبْدِ ، ثُمَّ يُقْضَى دَيْنُ سَيِّدِهِ ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ إِلَى مَا بَقِيَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ فَيَعْتِقُ ثُلُثُهُ وَيَبْقَى ثُلُثَاهُ لِلْوَرَثَةِ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ جِنَايَةَ الْعَبْدِ هِيَ أَوْلَى مِنْ دَيْنِ سَيِّدِهِ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ إِذَا هَلَكَ وَتَرَكَ عَبْدًا مُدَبَّرًا قِيمَتُهُ خَمْسُونَ وَمِائَةُ دِينَارٍ ، وَكَانَ الْعَبْدُ قَدْ شَجَّ رَجُلًا حُرًّا مُوضِحَةً عَقْلُهَا خَمْسُونَ دِينَارًا وَكَانَ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْعَبْدِ مِنَ الدَّيْنِ خَمْسُونَ دِينَارًا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 فَإِنَّهُ يُبْدَأُ بِالْخَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا الَّتِي فِي عَقْلِ الشَّجَّةِ ، فَتُقْضَى مِنْ ثَمَنِ الْعَبْدِ ، ثُمَّ يُقْضَى دَيْنُ سَيِّدِهِ ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ إِلَى مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ ، فَيَعْتِقُ ثُلُثُهُ ، وَيَبْقَى ثُلُثَاهُ لِلْوَرَثَةِ ، فَالْعَقْلُ أَوْجَبُ فِي رَقَبَتِهِ مِنْ دَيْنِ سَيِّدِهِ ، وَدَيْنُ سَيِّدِهِ أَوْجَبُ مِنَ التَّدْبِيرِ الَّذِي إِنَّمَا هُوَ وَصِيَّةٌ فِي ثُلُثِ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ ، فَلَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَجُوزَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ التَّدْبِيرِ وَعَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُدَبَّرِ دَيْنٌ لَمْ يُقْضَ ، وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ وَصِيَّةٌ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى ، قَالَ : /4 مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَى بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ سورة النساء آية 12 /4 /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 فَإِنْ كَانَ فِي ثُلُثِ الْمَيِّتِ مَا يَعْتِقُ فِيهِ الْمُدَبَّرُ كُلُّهُ ، عَتَقَ وَكَانَ عَقْلُ جِنَايَتِهِ دَيْنًا عَلَيْهِ يُتَّبَعُ بِهِ بَعْدَ عِتْقِهِ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْعَقْلُ الدِّيَةَ كَامِلَةً ، وَذَلِكَ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى سَيِّدِهِ دَيْنٌ /10 . وَقَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْمُدَبَّرِ إِذَا جَرَحَ رَجُلًا فَأَسْلَمَهُ سَيِّدُهُ إِلَى الْمَجْرُوحِ ، ثُمَّ هَلَكَ سَيِّدُهُ وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ وَلَمْ يَتْرُكْ مَالًا غَيْرَهُ ، فَقَالَ الْوَرَثَةُ : نَحْنُ نُسَلِّمُهُ إِلَى صَاحِبِ الْجُرْحِ ، وَقَالَ صَاحِبُ الدَّيْنِ : أَنَا أَزِيدُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ : /10 إِنَّهُ إِذَا زَادَ الْغَرِيمُ شَيْئًا فَهُوَ أَوْلَى بِهِ ، وَيُحَطُّ عَنِ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الدَّيْنُ قَدْرُ مَا زَادَ الْغَرِيمُ عَلَى دِيَةِ الْجَرْحِ ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَزِدْ شَيْئًا لَمْ يَأْخُذْ الْعَبْدَ /10 . وَقَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْمُدَبَّرِ إِذَا جَرَحَ وَلَهُ مَالٌ ، فَأَبَى سَيِّدُهُ أَنْ يَفْتَدِيَهُ : /10 فَإِنَّ الْمَجْرُوحَ يَأْخُذُ مَالَ الْمُدَبَّرِ فِي دِيَةِ جُرْحِهِ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ وَفَاءٌ اسْتَوْفَى الْمَجْرُوحُ دِيَةَ جُرْحِهِ وَرَدَّ الْمُدَبَّرَ إِلَى سَيِّدِهِ ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ وَفَاءٌ اقْتَضَاهُ مِنْ دِيَةِ جُرْحِهِ ، وَاسْتَعْمَلَ الْمُدَبَّرَ بِمَا بَقِيَ لَهُ مِنْ دِيَةِ جُرْحِهِ /10 *

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding the umm al-walad (slave mother of a child) who causes injury: The compensation for that injury is binding upon her master in his wealth, unless the compensation for that injury is more than the value of the umm al-walad. In that case, her master is not required to pay more than her value. That is because when the owner of a male slave or female slave hands over his slave or his female slave for an injury caused by one of them, he is not liable for more than that, even if the compensation is great. When the master of the umm al-walad cannot hand her over due to what has been established in the Sunnah regarding that, then when he pays her value, it is as if he handed her over. He is not liable for more than that. This is the best that I have heard, and he is not required to bear more than her value from her crime.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 ، فِي أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ تَجْرَحُ : /10 إِنَّ عَقْلَ ذَلِكَ الْجَرْحِ ضَامِنٌ عَلَى سَيِّدِهَا فِي مَالِهِ ، إِلا أَنْ يَكُونَ عَقْلُ ذَلِكَ الْجَرْحِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ قِيمَةِ أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ ، فَلَيْسَ عَلَى سَيِّدِهَا أَنْ يُخْرِجَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ قِيمَتِهَا ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ رَبَّ الْعَبْدِ أَوِ الْوَلِيدَةِ ، إِذَا أَسْلَمَ غُلامَهُ أَوْ وَلِيدَتَهُ بِجُرْحٍ أَصَابَهُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا ، فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ، وَإِنْ كَثُرَ الْعَقْلُ ، فَإِذَا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ سَيِّدُ أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَهَا ، لِمَا مَضَى فِي ذَلِكَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ ، فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا أَخْرَجَ قِيمَتَهَا فَكَأَنَّهُ أَسْلَمَهَا ، فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ . وَهَذَا أَحْسَنُ مَا سَمِعْتُ ، وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ مِنْ جِنَايَتِهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ قِيمَتِهَا /10 . /1 كِتَاب الْحُدُودِ /1

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned to him that a man and woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning?' They said: 'We disgrace them and they are flogged.' Abdullah ibn Salam said: 'You have lied, indeed stoning is in it (the Torah).' So they brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them placed his hand over the verse of stoning, then read what was before it and what was after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him: 'Lift your hand.' So he lifted his hand, and there was the verse of stoning. They said: 'He has spoken truthfully, O Muhammad, the verse of stoning is in it.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered regarding them both, and they were stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said: I saw the man leaning over the woman, protecting her from the stones. Malik said: Meaning he leans, bending over her until the stones fall upon him.

حَدَّثَنَا /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 نَافِعٍ L7863 /94 ، /27 عَنْ /93 عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ L4967 /93 ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : جَاءَتْ الْيَهُودُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَذَكَرُوا لَهُ أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْهُمْ وَامْرَأَةً زَنَيَا ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : /20 " مَا تَجِدُونَ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ فِي شَأْنِ الرَّجْمِ ؟ " فَقَالُوا : نَفْضَحُهُمْ وَيُجْلَدُونَ . فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَلَامٍ : كَذَبْتُمْ ، إِنَّ فِيهَا الرَّجْمَ . فَأَتَوْا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ ، فَنَشَرُوهَا ، فَوَضَعَ أَحَدُهُمْ يَدَهُ عَلَى آيَةِ الرَّجْمِ ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ مَا قَبْلَهَا وَمَا بَعْدَهَا ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَلَامٍ : ارْفَعْ يَدَكَ . فَرَفَعَ يَدَهُ ، فَإِذَا فِيهَا آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ ، فَقَالُوا : صَدَقَ يَا /55 مُحَمَّدُ /55 ، فِيهَا آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ ، فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَرُجِمَا /27 . فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ : فَرَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ يَحْنِي عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يَعْنِي يَحْنِي يُكِبُّ عَلَيْهَا حَتَّى تَقَعَ الْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهِ /10 *

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that a man from the tribe of Aslam came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and said to him: 'Indeed, the other (meaning himself) has committed adultery.' Abu Bakr said to him: 'Have you mentioned this to anyone other than me?' He said: 'No.' Abu Bakr said to him: 'Then repent to Allah and conceal yourself with Allah's concealment, for indeed Allah accepts repentance from His servants.' But his soul did not leave him in peace until he came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said to him the same as what he had said to Abu Bakr. Umar said to him the same as what Abu Bakr had said to him. But his soul did not leave him in peace until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: 'Indeed, the other has committed adultery.' Sa'id said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him three times, each time the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him. When he persisted with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to his family and said: 'Is he sick, or does he have madness?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, he is healthy.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Is he unmarried or married?' They said: 'Rather, he is married, O Messenger of Allah.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered regarding him, and he was stoned.

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah that he informed him that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him that she had committed adultery while she was pregnant. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Go until you give birth.' When she gave birth, she came to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Go until you nurse him.' When she nursed him, she came to him. He said: 'Go and entrust him to someone's care.' So she entrusted him to someone's care, then she came. Then he ordered regarding her, and she was stoned.

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani that they both informed him that two men brought a dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them said: 'O Messenger of Allah, judge between us by the Book of Allah.' The other, who was more knowledgeable, said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, judge between us by the Book of Allah, and permit me to speak.' He said: 'Speak.' He said: 'My son was a hired worker for this man, and he committed adultery with his wife. They informed me that my son deserves stoning, so I ransomed him with one hundred sheep and a slave girl of mine. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that my son deserves one hundred lashes and banishment for a year, and that stoning is only for his wife.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will surely judge between you by the Book of Allah. As for your sheep and your slave girl, they are returned to you.' Then he flogged his son one hundred times and banished him for a year. He ordered Unays al-Aslami to go to the wife of the other man, and if she confesses, stone her. She confessed, so he stoned her. Malik said: Al-'Asif means the hired worker.

hadiths.english_translation: FIRST NARRATION: Narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar from Abu Waqid al-Laythi that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was in Syria and mentioned to him that he found a man with his wife. Umar ibn al-Khattab sent Abu Waqid al-Laythi to his wife to question her about that. He came to her while there were women around her. He mentioned to her what her husband had said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and informed her that she would not be taken by his statement. He began prompting her with similar things so that she would retract, but she refused to retract and persisted in the confession. So Umar ordered regarding her, and she was stoned. SECOND NARRATION: Narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he heard him saying: When Umar ibn al-Khattab returned from Mina, he made his camel kneel at al-Abtah, then he piled up a pile of pebbles, then threw his cloak over it and lay down. Then he raised his hands to the sky and said: 'O Allah, I have become old, my strength has weakened, and my flock has spread. So take me to You without being negligent or excessive.' Then he came to Medina and addressed the people, saying: 'O people, the Sunan have been established for you, the obligations have been prescribed for you, and you have been left upon clarity unless you lead people astray right and left' - and he struck one of his hands against the other. Then he said: 'Beware lest you perish regarding the verse of stoning, that someone says: We do not find two punishments in the Book of Allah. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, were it not that people would say Umar ibn al-Khattab added to the Book of Allah the Exalted, I would have written it: The old man and the old woman, stone them both absolutely, for indeed we recited it.'
